summary.intent: Push new checkpoints, set up Neatlogs detections for scenario-sweep findings, log the day's summary in Obsidian, and run the P2/P3 scenario sweep. When the sweep crashed, find the cause and harden the app.
summary.outcome: Detections were created, the Obsidian notes were updated, and the P2/P3 run finished with an error. The renderer crash was investigated, and safety fixes were committed: a shell command guard that stops the agent killing unrelated Mac processes, a new stop_background tool, and renderer-crash window auto-reload. The root cause of the crash was not confirmed.

repo: The sweep agent has the Bash tool disabled, so every command goes through the runtime `shell` tool. One guard there covers all commands. `start_background` needed the same guard added separately.
Runtimes (local and SSH) share an interface in src/main/runtime/types.ts. Adding `stopBackground` meant changing types.ts, local.ts and ssh.ts together.
Startup resets states left stuck by an earlier crash, so crash recovery can rely on that logic.
Static loading of the large project uses only ~150 MB of renderer memory. The crash therefore builds up during a live run or comes from a single abnormal message.

code.finding: createWindow now reloads the window after a renderer crash. It was tested by deliberately crashing the renderer.
The `shell` tool blocks commands that could kill unrelated host processes. A `stop_background` tool was added, and `start_background` got the same guard.

workflow: Check macOS crash reports and measure memory before guessing at a crash cause.
Some sweep "bugs" are product choices, such as not showing the time in comment dates. Separate them from real bugs in the report.
Run two apps' sweeps one after the other so their ports don't clash.
A detection regex that is too broad should be narrowed to a specific pattern. The auth and account-security detection is an example.
A daily-note link written with a heredoc or append landed at the bottom of the page. Check where it was inserted.
